Summary of the completed work: analysis.py implements the coupled Farquhar/Collatz (C4) + Ball-Berry land-surface convention exactly as specified (hard-minimum A = min(Wc,Wj,We) − Rd, C4 branches Wc=Vcmax, Wj=alpha_q*APAR, We=4000*Vcmax*Ci/p_atm; CLM/Noah-MP Q10 Vcmax with high-temperature inhibition; Vcmax25_eff = vcmax25*n_factor*btran with Rd = 0.015*Vcmax_eff; Tetens/Bolton esat; h_s bounded to [0.25, 1]; b0 not btran-scaled; the stated 1.37/1.65 diffusion chain with A_mol = A*1e-6 and cf = p_atm/(R*T)). The coupled fixed point is solved by damped Picard iteration on Ci (damping 0.5, tolerance |ΔCi| < 1e-6 Pa or relative 1e-8), with a final chain pass so all reported variables form one common fixed point. Deliverables: results/leaf_fluxes.csv — 120 rows matching forcing.csv, columns time_hr,A_sun,A_shade,rs_sun,rs_shade,ci_sun,ci_shade,gs_sun,gs_shade, 0 NaNs, all finite, max fixed-point residual 0; results/case_convergence.csv — 5 rows, all converging to ci_final = 31.186759 Pa, A_final = 39.174336 umol/m2/s, rs_final = 167.513407 s/m (single attractor; n_iterations 25/25/23/26/27 from the supplied ci_init guesses under the stated criterion); results/diurnal.png — 1200×820 two-panel figure of A and rs for sunlit (red) and shaded (green) leaves over 0–119 h. Diurnal behavior: daytime Vcmax-limited regime (row 12: Wc = 39.77 binding vs Wj = 329.86, We = 48.96), so sunlit and shaded A coincide in 105/120 rows and diverge only at dawn/dusk where the shaded leaf is light-limited; nights give A = −Rd ∈ [−0.436, −0.225] (exact to 5.6e-17), gs = b0, rs up to 1082 s/m. Cross-validation: scipy brentq on f(ci) = chain(ci) − ci reproduces the Picard fixed point to 5.9e-9 Pa; Picard converges to the same point from ci_init spanning 1e-6 to 400 Pa.
